9uvzle:652: Why does all the knowledge you process with AI never "stick"? Let's start with a scenario you're definitely familiar with. You take a dozens-of-pages industry report, hand it to ChatGPT, and ask it to extract the key points. After twenty minutes of chatting, the ideas are clearly organized, even with its own analysis. You close the dialog, satisfied. The next day, you want to cite one of those data points. You open a new chat window, re-upload the report, re-ask the question—everything starts from scratch. That brilliant insight from last week's conversation? Gone. Those three papers you had AI compare last month? You have to redo it all. This problem bothered me for a long time. Until last month, Karpathy posted a long thread that explained it thoroughly. The way most people use AI to process documents today is essentially RAG—whether you know the term or not. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), in plain language, means: you throw a bunch of files in, and every time you ask a question, AI searches the files for relevant snippets and pieces together an answer for you. ChatGPT's file upload is RAG, Google's NotebookLM is RAG, and most enterprise knowledge-base solutions are RAG too. Does it work? Yes. But there's a fatal problem—knowledge doesn't accumulate.
